extracted.intended_audience: research software projects, open science platform builders, community organizations, and applicants seeking CZI Open Science grants
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Open Science program priorities and the types of projects they fund — focused on enabling open, reproducible, accessible scientific tools, platforms, and communities. Useful for applicants and ecosystem builders to align proposals with CZI funding goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance universal and immediate open sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI’s Open Science program aims to advance the universal and immediate open sharing of all scientific knowledge, processes, and outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is directed to projects that enable rapid, open dissemination of scientific results, methods, and resources so others can build on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make scientific outputs open and reproducible
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in tools, platforms, and organizations that help expand participation and access to the scientific process by making it open and reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize projects that improve reproducibility of analyses, workflows, data, and software (e.g., reproducible pipelines, metadata preservation, verifiable workflows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand participation and access to the scientific process
rubrics_metrics.description: Help expand participation and access to the scientific process by making it open and reproducible, and helping scientists build on each others’ work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support proposals that lower barriers for diverse groups to participate (training, onboarding, community outreach, localized resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund tools, platforms, and organizations that enable open science
rubrics_metrics.description: To this aim, we invest in tools, platforms, and organizations that help expand participation and access to the scientific process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible projects include libraries, platforms, infrastructure, community organizations, and services that materially support the open science ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support preprints and rapid open dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting preprints and open, rapid dissemination in the life sciences (bioRxiv and medRxiv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor infrastructure or services that accelerate and broaden access to preprints, early sharing, and open commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability, maintenance, and long-term project health
rubrics_metrics.description: Support ongoing maintenance, refactoring, and sustainability work to secure long-term health of widely used open-source scientific projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is appropriate for maintenance backlogs, refactoring for sustainability, and activities that create durable project governance and contributor pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community building, onboarding, and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Support onboarding, inclusion, and retention of people from historically marginalized groups and structurally improve community dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mentorship, contributor workshops, community roles (e.g., community champions), and programs that broaden contributor diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and internationalization / localization
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase accessibility of open platforms and localize software/documentation to non-English languages (e.g., localization to Spanish/Portuguese, translation infrastructure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize work that removes language and disability barriers: UI accessibility affordances, multilingual tutorials, culturally sensitive translation, and features to benefit low-vision/blind users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability, APIs, and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance interoperability within ecosystems via standards, APIs, and shared formats (e.g., Array API adoption, data format standards like Zarr, LinkML modeling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund projects that provide stable APIs, cross-project compatibility, and community processes for evolving standards and compliance measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation, education, and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide high-quality training, outreach, tutorials, and documentation to grow and support user and developer communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize community-led training, localized materials, workshops, and teaching resources that increase adoption and correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portability and reproducible workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable portability of complex biomedical workflows across clouds and on-premise environments (e.g., Common Workflow Language, Nextflow, Snakemake).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund tools and examples that make analyses portable, containerized, and reproducible across platforms and infrastructures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance, scalability, and modern hardware support
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve performance and scalability (e.g., GPU acceleration, multi-threading, out-of-core/cloud-based analysis) for large-scale scientific computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support backend improvements, parallelization, and adaptations to new architectures to enable handling of large datasets and faster analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous integration, testing, and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish/extend continuous integration, testing frameworks, and validation suites to ensure robustness and reproducibility (e.g., nightly CI, testing for BWA/BWA-MEM2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should include automated tests, validation datasets, and CI processes that increase trust and enable maintainers to release confidently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability, user experience, and debuggability
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve user experience, debuggability, and overall usability of scientific tools (e.g., pip resolver UX, Spyder remote support, UCSC Xena redesign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in UX design, clearer APIs, improved error handling, and documentation that makes tools more approachable to diverse user bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration and ecosystem compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate tools across the ecosystem to reduce technical debt and increase reuse (e.g., integrating ilastik with napari and Dask; scikit-image API improvements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund work that creates connectors, shared data models, and plugins so projects interoperate smoothly within scientific stacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source development, maintenance, and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Support open-source projects via maintenance, contributor recruitment, governance improvements, and community processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize activities that grow contributor bases, improve governance, and make projects sustainable and welcoming to new maintainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education & capacity building for under-resourced regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Build sustainable training infrastructure, accredited trainers, and regional capacity (e.g., LMICs in Africa, Latin America workshops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that create local training programs, accredited curricula, or regional hubs to increase local scientific computing capacity are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity & inclusion programs and pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund programs (D&I) aimed at recruiting, funding, mentoring, and creating pathways for historically underrepresented groups (e.g., residencies, internships, apprenticeships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support mentorship programs, internships, and targeted recruitment to diversify talent pipelines in open science and software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platforms for sharing methods, protocols, and peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Support sharing platforms that make methods and reviews discoverable and machine-readable (e.g., protocols.io, DocMaps, ReviewR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund infrastructure that documents methods, enables community review, and makes editorial processes transparent and machine-discoverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve data and metadata findability and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance metadata, identifiers, and resource linking (e.g., RRIDs, DataCite, tximeta) to make datasets, software, and resources discoverable and reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that enable consistent metadata capture, identifiers, and linking between papers and resources improve reproducibility and credit assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship, internships, and contributor training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Support apprenticeship and internship programs to train maintainers and increase participation from underrepresented groups (e.g., Apache Arrow apprenticeship, Outreachy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund programs that recruit, train, and transition new contributors into sustained maintainer roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics, dashboards, and measurement infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Build infrastructure for measuring compliance, maintenance, and other operational metrics (e.g., API compliance, maintenance dashboards for conda-forge/bioconda).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that create transparent metrics systems help prioritize maintenance, transparency, and sustainable practices across ecosystems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on domain-specific needs and translational impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Support projects that address specific domain workflows and translational use cases (e.g., clinical data extraction for LMICs, tools for microscopy, neuroimaging pipelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund work that tailors general open-science infrastructure to the practical needs of specific research communities and clinical/diagnostic use cases.
